subject: HelioBank POC: traffic intake and burst-probe plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Ng <rachel@heliobank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelioBank POC: traffic intake and burst-probe plan

Hi Rachel — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared onboarding plan for the POC (goal: validate latency & cost at HelioBank traffic patterns and confirm a production blueprint).

Key asks / confirmations we need from your side to size the trial:
- Nominal steady-state RPS (requests/sec) and typical daily distribution windows.
- Expected peak/burst patterns (peak RPS, duration, frequency).
- Typical input prompt token length and average response token length (we use these for token-cost modeling).
- Concurrency targets (how many parallel user sessions or simultaneous API connections you expect).
- Any streaming requirements (do you need chunked token streaming for UX?).
- Critical success criteria (latency p95 target, throughput targets, SLA tradeoffs, quality checks).

What we propose for the POC (high level):
- Baseline week: run steady-state at your nominal RPS to collect latency/throughput/cost and warm KV caches.
- Burst-probe week: apply scripted bursts matching your worst-case windows (we’ll coordinate exact windows).
- Acceptance gates: latency p95 <= 200ms for interactive flows OR sustained throughput of X tokens/sec with < 1% error rate; quality sanity checks on a canonical prompt set you provide.
- Owners: Helio technical lead (Rachel) + Redwood SE (Karthik) + Redwood AE (Vivek).
- Timeline suggestion: kickoff and data handoff this week, baseline run next week, burst week the week after — flexible if you need to shift.

Attached: helio_traffic_template.csv (simple CSV for the team to fill in RPS/burst windows/token lengths). Please fill in columns for local TZ, sample endpoints, and a few representative prompts (sanitized).

Next steps: please fill and return the template, and confirm a 60–90 minute kickoff slot this week so we can lock in the script windows and owners.

Thanks — Vivek

From: Rachel Ng <rachel@heliobank.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <viv@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@heliobank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelioBank POC: traffic intake and burst-probe plan

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the clear plan. I filled the template with our initial numbers (attached). Summary here so it’s easy to read:
- Nominal RPS: 25 req/sec across our chat endpoints (mostly business hours 8am–6pm PST).
- Recurring bursts: up to 150 req/sec for ~45s every 60–90 minutes during batch reconciliation windows.
- Prompt lengths (sanitized avg): 120 tokens in; responses ~320 tokens on average.
- Concurrency: typical active sessions 10–20; back-end fan-out can create short spikes to 40 concurrent requests for <2 minutes.
- Streaming: not required for the MVP — a full response per request is fine for now.

Success criteria we want to validate:
- p95 latency under 300ms for common conversational flows (we can be flexible if you recommend stronger targets).
- No data loss or >1% error rate during bursts.
- Cost-per-1k-token estimate within 20% of your forecast for the given profile.

Kickoff: we’re available Tue 4/20 or Wed 4/21 morning PST. Also adding Amit (infra) who will own test orchestration on our side.

Attached: helio_traffic_filled.csv (sanitized). Let us know if you need sample traces or more granular timing for the bursts.

—Rachel
Rachel Ng

rachel@heliobank.com | +1 212-555-0165

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Ng <rachel@heliobank.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <viv@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelioBank POC: traffic intake and burst-probe plan

Thanks Rachel — the numbers are helpful. A few technical clarifications from the SE side so we prepare the right probing harness and deployment:

1) KV cache behavior: do you have a set of highly-repeated prefixes (templates) we should pre-warm? If so, please flag them in the CSV. Pre-warm can materially reduce tail latency during bursts.
2) Tokenization sanity: you listed average lengths; do you have 95th percentile token sizes for both prompts and responses? We use those for memory footprint planning.
3) Trace samples: if possible, upload 10–20 sanitized request/response examples to the Drive folder (link below). We only need plaintext — please scrub PII. This helps us validate tokenizer behaviour and typical sequence lengths.
4) Embeddings / reranking: will any flows call embeddings or secondary reranking endpoints in the same request path? If yes, call graphs matter for concurrency.
5) Session stickiness: are sessions bound to a single client connection (affects KV cache hit expectations)?

We’ll provision a dedicated trial queue for HelioBank and run a baseline 72-hour steady-state followed by three scheduled burst windows (we’ll coordinate exact times during kickoff). I’ve added a short checklist in the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Helio-POC-samples

If you can drop the 95p token sizes and a few sample traces, we’ll lock the probe scripts and produce an initial capacity estimate ahead of kickoff.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Subject: Re: HelioBank POC: traffic intake and burst-probe plan

Great — thanks for the fast responses. Short action list and timeline to confirm:

1) Rachel/Amit: drop the 95th-percentile token sizes + 10 sample sanitized traces into the Drive folder (link above) by EOD Mon 4/21.
2) Redwood (Karthik): produce initial capacity estimate + probe script draft by Tue 4/22.
3) Kickoff: Tue 4/20 10:00–11:30am PST (Zoom link below). If you prefer Wed, tell us and we’ll move.
4) Baseline run: target window 4/25–4/27. Burst-probe week: 5/2–5/6 (contingent on trace review).

Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- p95 latency <= 250ms for primary conversational endpoints during baseline; during bursts we accept up to 400ms p95 if error rate stays <1%.
- No functional regressions on canonical prompt set; quality regressions flagged in the eval report.

I’ve linked the HubSpot deal and a mutual action doc (drop-in for timelines/acceptance gates). You’ll see the Deal ID RB-2027-1297 in HubSpot.
